result.note: Tests the 150-day tariff pause deadline, the reciprocal safeguard clause in the draft framework, and the US official leading the talks. Speculative G7 outcomes are skipped.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India–US trade negotiations as of June 2026:
items: The US pause on higher reciprocal tariffs runs for 150 days and expires on 24 July 2026.
The draft interim framework includes a reciprocal safeguard clause allowing either side to adjust tariffs if the other changes its commitments.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both statements are correct. Washington's 150-day pause ends on 24 July, and the draft framework carries a reciprocal safeguard clause. Both governments want an interim deal in place before the deadline, while work continues on the broader Bilateral Trade Agreement.
questions.source: The real deadline is July 24 when Washington's 150-day pause on higher reciprocal tariffs expires.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, which US official was scheduled to visit India for talks with Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal on an interim trade deal?
questions.explain: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer was scheduled to visit India on 23–24 June 2026. The visit followed negotiations earlier that month covering goods trade, non-tariff barriers, customs cooperation, trade facilitation and economic security.
questions.source: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer will visit India on June 23–24 for talks with Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal aimed at closing an interim trade deal before a key tariff deadline.
